definitions.explanation: A physical item given as a reward for winning a competition, contest, lottery, or other achievement.

examples.japanese: {一等|いっとう}の{賞品|しょうひん}は{旅行券|りょこうけん}だった。
examples.english: The first prize was a travel voucher.

examples.japanese: くじ{引|び}きで{豪華|ごうか}な{賞品|しょうひん}が{当|あ}たって、とてもうれしかった。
examples.english: I was so happy to win a luxurious prize in the raffle.

notes:
Composed of {賞|しょう} (prize, reward) and {品|ひん} (goods, article). Refers specifically to the physical item awarded as a prize.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {賞品|しょうひん}を{渡|わた}す: to hand over a prize
- {賞品|しょうひん}が{当|あ}たる: to win a prize
- {豪華|ごうか}な{賞品|しょうひん}: a luxurious prize
- {賞品|しょうひん}を{用意|ようい}する: to prepare prizes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {賞品|しょうひん}: prize (item) — the physical object given as a reward
- {商品|しょうひん}: merchandise, product — a homophone with completely different meaning
- {賞金|しょうきん}: prize money — monetary rather than physical reward
- {景品|けいひん}: freebie, giveaway — a promotional item, often from stores or events
- {トロフィー}: trophy — specifically a cup or figurine

NOTE:
Be careful not to confuse with the homophone {商品|しょうひん} (merchandise/product), which is much more common in daily life.
